text:
maria: Hey @people-ops — I noticed my 401(k) YTD contributions show $24,000 for 2025 but I only elected $22,500. Looks like employer match got accidentally recorded as employee deferral. Can someone advise on tax treatment and next steps? Concerned about W-2 reporting and deadlines.

jamal (payroll): Thanks @maria — can you DM your last paystub to payroll ops? Also confirm: traditional pre-tax or Roth? We need to verify whether the system double-counted match into elective deferrals. Tagging @alex-finance.

maria: DM sent with the paystub PDF. Plan = traditional pre-tax. On the paystub lines it shows `YTD_elective_deferrals: 24000` and `YTD_employer_match: 1800` but the per-pay details make it look like $192.31 employee + $115.38 match got added to employee deferral on a few checks.

alex-finance: Heads up — per IRS rules, if elective deferrals exceed the annual limit the excess must be distributed to the employee and reported on the W-2 for the year contributed. If corrected by Apr 15 following the calendar year, the distribution is includible in gross income for the year contributed but avoids certain compliance penalties. We'll coordinate with payroll to issue corrective distribution and update W-2/W-2C if needed.

jamal (payroll): Investigated — system math shows $1,500 excess deferral for 2025 due to a mapping bug on employer match lines. Options: 1) Process corrective distribution of the $1,500 (taxable in 2025, reported on W-2) and withhold standard taxes, then issue W-2C if necessary. 2) There's no recharacterization option for pre-tax elective deferrals. We'll default to corrective distribution. @maria, do you want standard withholding or do you prefer we withhold minimal and you handle estimated taxes?

maria: Standard withholding is fine. Can you confirm timing? I want to know if I'll need to file an amended return or if this will be handled via W-2C.

jamal (payroll): We'll process the corrective distribution in next payroll cycle (week of Jan 10). If processed before Apr 15, we will report the correction on the original W-2 (employee side) and issue a W-2C with updated amounts. You should not need to file an amended return for 2025 if the distribution is made and W-2/W-2C issued in time, but please consult your tax advisor.

lisa-peopleops: FYI we've pushed a fix to the plan admin mapping so future matches won't write to the elective deferral field. Running an audit for all 2025 records to find any other affected folks — will reach out individually if we find more issues :mag_right: :sorry:
notes: payroll-bot: distribution created ID 563210; amount $1,500; withholding fed 22% state 6% (est net $1,110)
